text:
Priya: ran into sustained tail latency on multi-tenant inference with host-offload enabled. repro attached: high churn + small allocations -> lots of tiny hostpages and fragmentation.
Gabe: do you have the allocation histogram? small pages probably killing our slab coalescer.
Priya: yes: 70% of frees are <8KB, but we only coalesce at 64KB boundary. results in many tiny host allocations + DMA mapping overhead.
Rox: hmm that points to allocator granularity mismatch between GPU staging slabs and OS page sizes. options: subpage packing vs compacting background thread.
Gabe: subpage packing complicates eviction bookkeeping; compacting thread could throttle but adds pause risk on heavy churn.
Priya: another idea: introduce a small-object cache for host-backed pages that reuses freed small pages per-tenant to avoid repeated mmap/munmap. cheap and local.
Rox: per-tenant small-page cache + periodic scavenger sounds reasonable. need to guard against long-tail memory retention. add max-resident-per-tenant param.
Gabe: also consider batching hostmaps for contiguous small allocations into a single mmap and expose sub-offsets. avoids many DMA ops.
Priya: agree. batch-mmaps + per-tenant small cache as first step. we'll avoid subpage allocator complexity initially.
infra-bot: canary deploy queued: canary/smallpage-cache-probe -> staging (4 GPUs), ETA 6m
Rox: I'll file a short RFC follow-up with tradeoffs and the scavenger heuristics. Gabe, can you add perf counters for small-page reuse rate and DMA-op count?
Gabe: yes. Priya: I'll land a prototype branch that implements per-tenant LRU cache with eviction thresholds. tests: stress-fuzz + multi-tenant mem-pressure.
Priya: thanks, will post results when canary finishes.
